name: Free Editorial Gemini
storyIdentity: KAREN ABANDONS CAR ON HIGHWAY & CALLS 911 AS UBER
rejectionReasonForMultiple: The source video contains 549s of raw footage with approximately 180s of active confrontation. Attempting to force 3 serialized parts (Part 1/2/3) produces 255s of runtime, requiring 75s of dead-air driving, circular flashbacks, and an early spoiler arrest at the start of Part 2. A single high-density 64.5s short preserves 100% causal momentum, delivers an explosive hook, and maximizes TikTok viral retention.
centralConflict: An entitled driver refuses police assistance, abandons her disabled sedan in a live highway lane, walks away into traffic, and repeatedly calls emergency 911 to demand roadside concierge service.
viewerQuestion: Can you actually get arrested for being rude to 911 after abandoning your car on the highway?

hook.quotedDialogue: Being rude is not illegal! / Misuse of 911.
hook.visualAction: Close-up through passenger window/grate: handcuffed woman loudly proclaims that being rude isn't a crime while officer calmly clicks handcuffs.

beats.purpose: Stop the scroll instantly with an outrageous, polarizing claim from the suspect.
beats.causalLinkToPrevious: Entry point: In medias res teaser establishing high friction before revealing the bizarre cause.
beats.visualAction: Suspect in blue top standing in handcuffs, yelling 'Being rude is not illegal!'
beats.openLoop: Why is this woman in handcuffs claiming being rude isn't illegal?

beats.purpose: Establish the high-stakes highway setting and the absurd catalyst.
beats.causalLinkToPrevious: Rewind to 20 minutes earlier: shows how the entire bizarre incident began.
beats.voiceoverText: Twenty minutes earlier on a packed Florida highway, this driver's car completely stalled in the fast lane. But when a deputy pulled up to help...
beats.visualAction: Cruiser pulls up behind stalled grey Camry blocking active highway traffic on US-19.
beats.openLoop: How does a simple stalled car lead to handcuffs?

beats.purpose: Show the immediate defiance and refusal of roadside assistance.
beats.causalLinkToPrevious: Deputy approaches to offer a push off the road, but meets aggressive defiance.
beats.visualAction: Deputy warns 'Continue with the attitude and I'll tow it myself.' Driver retorts 'Excuse me, you can do that' and storms away.
beats.openLoop: Did she really just abandon her car in the middle of highway traffic?

beats.purpose: Depict the shock of police and danger of an abandoned vehicle in live traffic.
beats.causalLinkToPrevious: Driver walks away into oncoming traffic; deputy is left holding the road.
beats.voiceoverText: She didn't just walk away—she left her vehicle blocking live traffic and called nine-one-one with a bizarre demand.
beats.visualAction: Driver walking down the road away from her car; deputies rush to push the Camry off the highway.

beats.purpose: Highlight the peak absurdity of abusing emergency dispatch like an Uber concierge.
beats.causalLinkToPrevious: While walking, she dials 911 to complain about her car and insults the operator.
beats.visualAction: Waveform graphic over aerial map of 911 recording: 'Where is my car? I'm going to hang up until I get somebody with a brain cell left!'

beats.purpose: Confrontation on the residential sidewalk where suspect claims she's calling Uber.
beats.causalLinkToPrevious: Deputies track down the 911 caller on a nearby residential street.
beats.visualAction: Deputy confronts her: 'Why do you keep calling 911?' Driver: 'To find out where my car went. I'm calling an Uber.'
beats.openLoop: Can she just walk away in an Uber?

beats.purpose: Deliver the satisfying consequence of illegal emergency line misuse.
beats.causalLinkToPrevious: Her refusal to cooperate and repeated 911 abuse exhaust all roadside discretion.
beats.visualAction: Deputy: 'We gave you the option to wait... we're past that now. Turn around.' Cuffs click on wrists: 'Misuse of 911.'
beats.openLoop: How does she react when placed in the paddy wagon?

beats.purpose: Deliver comedic and dramatic justice through her stubborn van argument.
beats.causalLinkToPrevious: Placed in the back of the transport van, she continues arguing through the screen.
beats.visualAction: Inside van: 'My car was being towed by 911!' Deputy: '911 is for emergencies like stabbings and shootings, ma'am.'

beats.purpose: Fast 3-second factual closure with no lingering dead air.
beats.causalLinkToPrevious: Legal resolution of the arrest charges.
beats.voiceoverText: She was booked on a five-thousand-dollar bond for misusing nine-one-one.
beats.visualAction: Official arrest record summary cleanly formatted over blurred background; fast cut to black.

evidenceLimitations: Original YouTube video has channel logo ('Police Ride-Alongs') and burned-in subtitles at bottom center. Optimal TikTok presentation requires dynamic 9:16 vertical crop to reframe suspects and officers while cropping out old YouTube text overlays.
